event_info.event_description: Analyze for disclosures on global pandemic risks. Look for corporate language discussing widespread impacts like supply chain disruptions, labor shortages, remote work transitions, and fundamental shifts in consumer demand.

holistic_analysis: EFX’s 10-K acknowledges that the COVID-19 pandemic is both a historical and an ongoing risk driver.  The filing states that the company “experienced significant revenue declines” in several markets because of the pandemic, demonstrating a direct, realised impact on its financial performance.  Management also warns that similar revenue contractions could recur with future pandemics, identifying a forward-looking exposure tied to macro-economic sensitivity in consumer credit demand and lending activity.  Although the narrative stops short of providing dollar figures or detailed operational disruptions (e.g., remote-work costs, supply-chain interruptions), it still elevates risk by expressly linking pandemic conditions to revenue shortfalls.  Given that COVID-19’s peak disruption began less than four years before the 2024 filing date, the Time Decay Principle allows moderately high scores (7-10) for direct, unquantified impacts and mid-range scores (3-6) for generic or background references.  Overall, the language reflects a material, recently-experienced risk that remains relevant, but the absence of precise metrics or granular operational details tempers the severity slightly below the maximum range.

evidence_list.snippet: Our business has been and may continue to be negatively impacted by health epidemics, pandemics and similar outbreaks.

components.reason: Admits past negative impact and persistence of the threat (‘has been and may continue’).
Statement is generic – no specifics on magnitude, functions or geography.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Provides a generic but explicit acknowledgement of pandemic impact; modest aggravation, limited detail.

evidence_list.snippet: We face various risks related to health epidemics, pandemics and similar outbreaks.

components.reason: Purely boiler-plate with no company-specific effects or metrics.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: High-level risk statement adds minimal incremental severity because it is fully generic.

evidence_list.snippet: For example, the COVID-19 pandemic and the mitigation efforts by governments to attempt to control its spread adversely impacted the global economy and led to reduced consumer spending and lending activities.

components.reason: Names COVID-19 explicitly and links it to reduced consumer spending and lending—core demand drivers for EFX’s products.
Impact framed at macroeconomic level, not quantified or tied solely to EFX.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Highlights mechanism of harm (lower spending/lending) but lacks firm-level metrics, yielding a moderate score.

evidence_list.snippet: Our customers, and therefore our business and revenues, are sensitive to negative changes in general economic conditions.

components.reason: Clarifies causal chain from macroeconomic downturn (including pandemic shocks) to EFX revenue.
Does not name COVID-19 explicitly and is broadly applicable to any downturn.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Adds context on sensitivity but remains indirect and generic; low incremental risk weight.

evidence_list.snippet: We experienced significant revenue declines in several of our markets as a result of COVID-19 and we may experience similar revenue declines as a result of future health epidemics, pandemics and similar outbreaks.

components.reason: Directly connects COVID-19 to ‘significant revenue declines’—a realised, material impact.
Flags possibility of repeat declines in future outbreaks (forward-looking exposure).
No numerical quantification of the revenue hit.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Strongest evidence: realised, company-specific financial impact and continuing risk, but unquantified, resulting in a high-moderate score.

evidence_list.snippet: • terrorist activity, natural disasters, pandemics and other catastrophic events;

components.reason: Includes pandemics in list of catastrophic events affecting international operations.
List format, fully generic, no detail or historical impact.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Only a cursory mention within a laundry list; negligible incremental severity after generic deduction.
